class.name: NNBTNodes
class.brief_description: Base class for all Noodle Nodes behaviour tree nodes.
class.description: Behaviour Trees are a commonly used structure that can be used to create artificial intelligence in games for the non-playable characters. A behaviour tree has a root node and under it a tree structure, where the branches of the tree define the behaviour for the AI. The utility enabled Behaviour Trees in Noodle Nodes GDExtension extend the traditional Behaviour Tree with utility functions. The Behaviour Tree nodes can be used as a regular behaviour tree, but the extended utility features allow you to add utility-based branch selection and execution of the Node Query System queries within your trees. The Behaviour Tree in Noodle Nodes GDExtension keeps its data in a typed [NNBlackboard] resource owned by the nearest root of any Noodle Nodes system, so the nodes of one tree share their data without any per-tick plumbing and nothing is passed as a tick argument. That board is authoritative for [method NoodleNodes.get_blackboard_resource], [method NoodleNodes.get_blackboard], [method NoodleNodes.set_blackboard], [method NoodleNodes.has_blackboard], [method NoodleNodes.erase_blackboard] and [method NoodleNodes.get_actor]. With no root ancestor the helpers return their default value, [code]false[/code] or [code]null[/code] without reporting errors. [NNBTNodeReference] resolves these helpers from its target's own position in the tree. Each node tracks a run lifecycle. A run starts with the [code]on_before_run[/code] hook the first time the node is ticked while no run is active, and it ends with either the [code]on_after_run[/code] hook (when the node returns [code]SUCCESS[/code] or [code]FAILURE[/code]) or the [code]on_interrupt[/code] hook (when the active run is abandoned). Every [code]on_before_run[/code] is matched by exactly one [code]on_after_run[/code] or [code]on_interrupt[/code] for the same run, and a node that never started a run receives no lifecycle callback. The [code]on_before_run[/code], [code]on_after_run[/code] and [code]on_interrupt[/code] script hooks are provided by [NNBTTaskNodes]; composite nodes participate in the run lifecycle internally only. The [code]SKIP[/code] result is not terminal: the run stays active until it completes or is interrupted. [method interrupt] is idempotent and does nothing when the node has no active run. Disabling a node interrupts and resets its subtree, so re-enabling the node starts a fresh run on the next tick.

method.name: get_is_running
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while a run is active. A run starts on the first tick while no run is active and ends with a terminal [code]SUCCESS[/code] or [code]FAILURE[/code] result, with [method interrupt], or with a disable, which interrupts and resets the node. A [code]SKIP[/code] result is not terminal, so the run stays active. The value is [code]false[/code] before the first tick and after a reset.

method.name: get_tree_root
method.description: Returns a relative node path to the furthest direct [NNBTNodes] ancestor.

method.name: interrupt
method.description: Force-stops the node's active run. Task nodes run their [code]on_interrupt[/code] script hook and every still-active behaviour tree child is interrupted as well. Calling it on a node without an active run is a safe no-op, so it is idempotent.

method.name: reset
method.description: Interrupts the active run of this node and its whole subtree, propagates the reset to every behaviour tree child, and clears node-lifetime state, such as a memory sequence's stored child, a limiter budget, or a run-once held result. Per-run state is initialised again when the next run starts. Disabling the node, or an ancestor, triggers the same reset.

members.member: Defines how enabled direct [NNConsiderations] child nodes (such as [NNConsideration], [NNConsiderationGroup] and [NNCustomPropertyConsideration]) are aggregated into [member score]. In the behaviour tree, only direct children of [NNBTScoreBasedPicker] are evaluated for their score. The default is [constant NoodleNodes.EVALUATION_MULTIPLY].
The score this node received from the Utility-based evaluation. Read-only runtime state: it is written by evaluation and is never saved with the scene.

The result of this node's most recent tick, written automatically by the node's tick handling. Read-only runtime state: the running-action query derives from it, so scripts cannot set it, and it is never saved with the scene.

constants.constant: The node has not finished yet and will be ticked again.
The node did not run. [NNBTSequence] and [NNBTSelector] move on to their next child, and [NNBTParallel] counts it as a success. The result is not terminal, so the node's run stays active.
